payload.message: UnboundLocalError: local variable 'count' referenced before assignment

viva.summary: The student demonstrates a strong grasp of object-oriented concepts, specifically the distinction between class and instance variables. They also show good intuition for defensive programming and input validation.

rubric.revise_next: Continue exploring object-oriented design by looking into how to make attributes private using double underscores.

questions.answer: Ye line count track karne ke liye hai ke total kitne accounts bane hain. Hum ise class name se is liye access karte hain kyunke ye ek class variable hai jo saare objects mein same rehta hai, self use karne se ye har object ka apna variable ban jata.
questions.feedback: Excellent explanation of class variables versus instance variables.
questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the line `Account.count = Account.count + 1` inside your __init__ method, and why do you access it via the class name instead of self?

questions.answer: Yeh line check karti hai ke deposit amount positive honi chahiye kyunke negative balance add karna logical nahi hai. Agar amount zero se kam hui toh yeh transaction nahi hogi.
questions.feedback: You correctly identified the need for input validation to maintain logical consistency.
questions.prompt: Explain in your own words what this line of your code does, and why it's needed: `if amount > 0:`

questions.answer: Sir, __init__ method mein hum if condition laga sakte hain ke agar balance zero se kam ho to usse zero set karde. Is tarah balance kabhi negative nahi hoga.
questions.feedback: Your proposed solution for handling negative initialization is logically sound and robust.
questions.prompt: If we wanted to ensure that the balance can never be negative even if someone tries to set it manually during initialization, what check would you add to the __init__ method?
